prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
U0020: A change in the routing and ETA of a single flight will impact the metering STA and delay for that aircraft, and may potentially impact the STA and delays of other aircraft in the sequence.
U0021: Tools for the Traffic Manager to evalaute the impact of arrival rerouting on STAs before the reroutes are implemented (i.e., a trial planner) are not currently available.
U0022: TBFM is unable to determine the impact of such changes until they actually take place.
U0023: This makes it very difficult for traffic managers to accurately evaluate the impact of any prospective change, especially when multiple flights are involved.
U0024: XM/CS operations may exacerbate the impact of convective weather on arrival metering operations due to schedule interactions between Metering Points. 4 PROPOSED SOLUTION (DRAW) The Dynamic Routes for Arrivals in Weather (DRAW) system is a trajectory-based decision support capability for traffic managers, and is aimed at improving arrival traffic flow.
U0025: DRAW aids Center Traffic Managers in identifying and evaluating route changes that improve arrival traffic flow efficiency and mitigate impact of weather constraints on their arrival metering operations [3].
U0026: DRAW combines the weather avoidance capability of NASA’s Dynamic Weather Routes (DWR) with arrival-specific rerouting algorithms [4].
U0027: The arrival-specific rerouting algorithm continuously searches for reroute opportunities as track and flight plan data are updated.
U0028: The DRAW’s route trial planning capability is integrated with arrival scheduling components to allow the Traffic Management Coordinators (TMCs) at Centers to evaluate the impact of proposed DRAW reroutes on arrival scheduling before implementing them (see Figure 1).
U0029: This integrated route and schedule trial planner could also be used by traffic managers to manually build and trial plan a route of their own choosing.
U0030: Figure 1: DRAW Operational Environment: Current Arrival Metering Operations 4.1 DRAW SYSTEM DESCRIPTION The DRAW system is intended to reside in Center Traffic Management Units (TMUs) as a decision support tool for TMCs.
U0031: DRAW is capable of providing route advisories early enough to be implemented before the flight reaches the scheduling freeze horizon (Figure 2), or in the case of XM/CS operations, after crossing a MP and before the downstream freeze horizon.
U0032: Rerouting a flight before the scheduling freeze horizon is operationally preferable because it allows the arrival scheduling system (e.g., TBFM) to adjust its STAs and resulting schedule delay before arrival controllers need to work the flight.
U0033: However, DRAW may be configured to provide route advisories for flights with frozen STAs; manual STA assignment or schedule rippling by the TMC may be necessary to accommodate such advisories, or they may be acceptable if the resultant delay is manageable within the existing schedule.
U0034: Due to the effect of weather uncertainty on trajectory predictions, this capability may be particularly useful in cases where the freeze horizon is especially long/distant.
U0035: Figure 2: DRAW Operational Time Horizon The DRAW interface utilizes two displays, a planview map display (e.g., Planview Graphical User Interface, PGUI) and a scheduling timeline display (e.g., Timeline Graphical User Interface, TGUI).
U0036: An example of the current DRAW interface is shown in Figure 3.
U0037: Key features include the DRAW Advisory List which displays proposed reroutes, and an integrated route and schedule trial planner that allows routes and corresponding schedule impact to be evaluated simultaneously.
U0038: ETAs STAs Trial Plan Flight Schedule and Delays DRAW Advisory List Figure 3: DRAW System Interface DRAW’s trajectory-based route trial planner functionality is implemented on the PGUI, which provides TMCs the ability to initiate a trial plan by modifying either a DRAW-proposed route or the flight’s current flight plan route (including the assigned Standard Terminal Arrival Route or STAR).
U0039: Modifications can be made to the point at which the flight deviates from the flight plan route (maneuver start point or MSP), the point at which the flight returns to the original flight plan route (return capture fix or RCF), and additional auxiliary waypoints.
U0040: The trial plan trajectory automatically updates the flight’s ETA, weather conflict status, and/or changes to the flight trajectory.
U0041: The PGUI may be displayed in both the ‘home TBFM’ ARTCC TMU as well as adjacent facilities.
U0042: DRAW trial planning functionality is available at each TBFM PGUI.
U0043: The impact of the trial plan route and the updated ETA on the meter point(s) and runway ETAs/STAs for all impacted flights are calculated by the integrated trial scheduler (embedded in the TBFM system), and displayed on the TGUI(s), without actually implementing the reroute.
